name: amp-loop-stability
description: Issue #10: bandgap_top servo-loop gain and stability margin with the offset-budgeted amp (design/bandgap_amp.sch). Single-injection loop-gain probe (exact for this topology's single-wire loop break -- see testbench header) swept 0.1 Hz - 2 GHz; the record's stability criterion is the worst-case (global-minimum) loop-gain magnitude across that sweep, not a classical 0dB-crossing phase margin (this topology's Bode response never crosses 0dB -- see design/bandgap_error_budget.md Sec 4).
claim: This design's own stability criterion (not a ratified spec line -- see design/bandgap_error_budget.md Sec 4): worst-case loop-gain magnitude over 0.1 Hz - 2 GHz stays >= 0 dB at every PVT corner.

pm_deg.description: This design's stability criterion (design/bandgap_error_budget.md Sec 4): phase margin -- the angular distance of T's phase (evaluated at the frequency of minimum loop-gain magnitude, the worst-case approach to the Nyquist critical point) from the critical point's phase for this topology's characteristic equation 1-T=0, i.e. 0 degrees (mod 360), not the textbook -180 degrees that applies to a 1+T=0 loop -- must stay >= 45 degrees (a standard minimum-PM bar) at every PVT corner.

dc_gain_db.description: Sanity floor, not a spec claim: the .ic seed must still be finding the intended nonzero-current operating point at every corner (AC analysis linearizes around whatever DC point converges; a collapse to the degenerate near-zero-current state -- Sec 4.2 of design/bandgap_operating_point.md -- would show up as near-zero small-signal gm everywhere and a much lower DC loop gain than any nonzero-current corner should show).
